lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Auto Parts | Mechanical Design Engineer | Metro City, Country | Jun 2025 - Present
- Designed stamping dies for automotive brackets in SolidWorks, cutting the scrap rate from 6% to 4% on two press lines.
- Ran tolerance stack-up analyses for 12 production parts and signed off first-article inspections with the supplier.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality, personal details that should be left off by convention.
items.because: They are not relevant to the candidate’s qualifications and use space.

items.says: The current Mechanical Design Engineer entry takes attention away from an ML/agent target.
items.because: As the lead experience entry, its mechanical-design focus pulls the reader away from that direction.

items.says: The role sequence does not explain the candidate’s career progression.
items.because: A reader may be unsure how the current Mechanical Design Engineer role fits after software engineering and an ML internship.

items.says: Education appears before Experience.
items.because: A reader looking for relevant work history must get past the degrees first.

items.says: The inspection work gives its scope but not its outcome.
items.because: The 12-part count shows reach, not what changed for fit, quality, or production.

items.says: The 35% accuracy gain has no comparison basis.
items.because: Without a baseline or whether the gain is relative or in percentage points, its size is difficult to interpret.

items.says: The routing design comes before its result.
items.because: That makes the improvement easy to miss.

items.says: The reductions in calls and latency come after the training method and a compressed comparison.
The claimed purpose of assistant-only loss masking is technically incorrect.
items.because: It excludes tool-output tokens from the training loss rather than directly training the model to reproduce them.

items.says: The bullet repeats the adapter method from the accuracy bullet without adding a distinct result.
items.because: It uses space without giving the reader another outcome or contribution to evaluate.

items.says: The feature-extraction description is unexplained and difficult for readers outside the team to interpret.
items.because: “ML-extracted features” does not show the technical approach, and “diagnostics triage branch” may not explain what the system does.

items.says: The backlog result is not the opening of the entry, although it is the strongest line.
items.because: Placing its concrete contribution and 68% result last makes them less likely to be seen on a quick scan.

items.says: The 4x GPU-memory reduction is overstated as an effect of switching from FP32 to BF16 alone.
items.because: BF16 uses half the storage per value, while total fine-tuning memory depends on other tensors and optimizer states.

items.says: The bullet shifts from past tense to present tense in a role that ended in July 2024.
items.because: “Adds” sounds like a current activity and conflicts with the role dates.

items.says: The three-day release-cycle duration has no prior duration for comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot judge how much the cycle improved.

items.says: The claim that the migration removed nightly backlogs gives no measure of the operational change.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how much backlogs or dispatch delays changed.

items.says: The migration result is not the opening of the entry, although it is the strongest line.
items.because: Leading with the 30-service migration and removal of dispatch-delaying backlogs would make their scale and result easier to notice.

items.says: The AI-practices claim gives neither a specific practice nor a checkable result, and it does not connect clearly to the runtime work.
items.because: A reader cannot picture what was introduced or see evidence of the claimed benefits, so the broad claim feels disconnected from the other bullets.

items.says: The 100x comparison leaves unclear what grew.
The 50-way test condition does not show how the failures were verified as resolved.
items.because: It gives the test scale but no result or before-and-after comparison supporting the reliability claim.

items.says: The concrete concurrency result is not the opening bullet of the project.
items.because: Putting it first would give a scanning reader a concrete example of the technical work.

items.says: The 0.89 correlation does not identify the two quantities being compared.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the evaluator’s scores were correlated with.

items.says: The result is buried after a long, jargon-heavy description of the trial conditions.
items.because: “Injected degradation” may be unclear outside the team, and the wording and ordering make the finding harder to scan.

items.says: The triage outcome appears misattributed, and its backlog figure conflicts with the result elsewhere.
items.because: The Mobility Systems bullet attributes a 68% reduction to the industrial inspection triage branch, while this project claims the same result as two-thirds.

items.says: The remaining triage description does not explain how screening changed case handling and relies on unclear jargon.
items.because: “Triage branch” and “ML-extracted features” do not make the system, method, or contribution to this evaluation project clear.
